items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: And at that time people like Freddie Hubbard and Wes Montgomery would occasionally drive down the 40 miles from Indianapolis over to the Trees Center

ctx.x: And was there jazz — was jazz recognized anywhere like it is now when you went there?

Oh no. They didn’t offer the saxophone and neither did the Manhattan School of Music. Now that was 1957. I think maybe in 1958 or ’59 they finally started the jazz band for I think a half a credit and you met three times a week I think. And Buddy Baker the trombone player was the leader of that. Yeah it took a while to get going and the practice rooms were at a place called East Hall, it was like a rectangle with a couple of rooms in the center but all the practice rooms on the outside, and he had a particular…

There’s something for me that — it was a sort of similar at SUNY Fredonia but this was years later when I was there, that when students are pursuing something that the administration in the school doesn’t do on their own, it’s actually more special.
